bodyEdits.source: Owner rule: no prices in a page body outside FAQ answers and blog posts. Each edit takes a dollar range out of a service body, keeping the rest of the sentence (and every link) as written; the Panels flat-rate sentence restates the live city pages' claim (migration/live-snapshots/locations_gilbert.html) in plain words (copy review, 2026-10-17: slop-services-081). Each `find` must occur exactly once in that service's body text and may not cut through a link; after the edits no service body may contain a price. The ranges stay in the cost FAQ answers.

edits.find: For a standard 200-amp like-for-like panel replacement in the Phoenix metro, expect $5,200 to $6,500. If your job needs a full service replacement with a new all-in-one meter base and panel combo, the range is typically $6,400 to $8,750. Larger 320 or 400-amp service upgrades climb from there.
edits.replace: We price panel work at a flat rate with no hidden fees. Ask us for a free quote.

edits.find: Most Tesla Wall Connector installs in the Valley run $650 to $1,800 depending on
edits.replace: The price of a Tesla Wall Connector install depends on

edits.find: For reference, a standard 200-amp like-for-like panel replacement in the Valley generally runs $5,200 to $6,500, and a full service replacement with a new all-in-one meter base and panel is typically $6,400 to $8,750.

The relevant number for comparison: adding capacity later, once the drywall is up and the meter is set, means a panel or full service replacement that generally runs $5,200 to $6,500 for a standard 200-amp like-for-like, or $6,400 to $8,750 for a full service replacement with a new all-in-one meter base and panel.
edits.replace: Adding capacity later, once the drywall is up and the meter is set, means a panel or full service replacement.

linkFixes.source: Links in a post, city body (`location`) or FAQ answer (`faq`, by question) that point to the wrong place. Owner rule: every free-estimate request goes to /estimate; these links ask for an estimate or a visit but don't say "free estimate", so the migration's phrase rule misses them (city and post CTAs to "/", the old homepage form: decision D5, 2026-10-17). A citation wrapped in a Google search URL goes to the page it names (decision D6), and the ROC lookup link to the Registrar's own host (decision D13). A citation whose page is gone with no current equivalent (`to`: null) keeps its words and loses the link (preview crawl M5). Each must match exactly one link by its text and target.
